title: Shapes behind an interface with a default method

blocks.text: An **interface** is a contract: implementing classes supply its abstract methods, and code written against the interface works with any of them. Since Java 8 an interface may also carry **default** methods, whose body implementers inherit and may override; a default method can call the interface's abstract methods. Records can implement interfaces too.
This is the course's own `Shape2` design. In `Areas`, write:

items: `Shape.display()`, a default method returning `"This is a shape with area: <area>"`, the area formatted with `String.format("%.2f", area)`.
`Circle(double radius)` and `Rectangle(double length, double width)` implement `calculateArea()` (`π·r²`, `length·width`) and keep the default `display()`.
The record `Square(double side)` implements `calculateArea()` and overrides `display()` to return `"A square with side <side>"`, the side formatted with `%.2f`.
`Areas.largest(List<? extends Shape> shapes)` returns the shape with the largest area, or `Optional.empty()` when there is none.

blocks.text: (`String.format` uses your default locale; the tests run with a `.` decimal separator.)

new Circle(5).calculateArea()       -> 78.539...
new Rectangle(4, 5).calculateArea() -> 20.0
new Rectangle(4, 5).display()       -> "This is a shape with area: 20.00"
new Circle(1).display()             -> "This is a shape with area: 3.14"
new Square(3).display()             -> "A square with side 3.00"
largest([Circle(3), Rectangle(3, 4), Square(2)]) -> Circle(3)   (28.27 beats 12.0 and 4.0)
largest([])                         -> Optional.empty()

cases.says: A circle and a rectangle compute their areas through the Shape interface, and the default display() reports each one's own area.
The Square record implements Shape and overrides display() with its own wording.
largest returns the shape with the biggest area, whatever class implements it.
largest of an empty list is an empty Optional.

concepts: A default method has a body that implementers inherit or override, and it can call the interface's abstract methods.
An interface is a contract its implementing classes fulfil, and code written against it works with any implementation.
Records can implement interfaces and so take part in polymorphic code.
